# SAR-1 reference set: openEMS's own SAR and MRI examples, run as their authors wrote them

What openEMS 0.37.0's own SAR and MRI tutorials computed, run unmodified on the version circuitRF tests, and kept as
fixed data (`docs/sonnet-briefs/brief-sar-1-openems-reference-set.md`). Every later phase of the SAR series gates
against these numbers. What they mean is in `docs/design/sar.md` §3. Produced on 2026-10-17.

**The data is not in the repository** (owner, 2026-10-18): it is kept on the developer machine, in the four folders
`.gitignore` names. What the repository holds is how it was made: this README (every file, the versions, the
commands) and `tools/`. Where the data is absent, `SarReferenceSetTests` skips with a reason, and the commands below
make it again.

**These are externally generated references** (CLAUDE.md §Validation expectations; overview L4). **Nothing here was
produced by circuitRF, and nothing here may be regenerated by it later.** The tutorials are openEMS's own scripts at
the `v0.37.0` tag, run unmodified by the wrappers in `tools/`. The wrappers are reference-generation material:
**nothing under `src/` or `tools/` may import, copy or call them** (the GPL boundary of
`testdata/em3d/f0/README.md`). openEMS's bundled phantom `.h5` files are not committed (overview L3).

## Layout

```
Dipole_SAR/       Python tutorial Dipole_SAR.py: 1 GHz dipole 20 mm from a three-layer ellipsoid head
MRI_Loop_Coil/    Python tutorial MRI_Loop_Coil.py: 7 T (298 MHz) loop beside the bundled ellipsoid head phantom
MRI_LP_Birdcage/  Octave tutorial MRI_LP_Birdcage.m: 3 T (128 MHz) 8-rung low-pass birdcage, quadrature feed
analytic/         test_sar_analytic.py's unittest log, and its two phantoms through the installed sar_calc
tools/            the wrappers that ran them (reference-generation material, see above)
```

Every `.npy` is a plain NumPy array (C order). Mesh lines are in **metres**. Complex arrays are complex128 unless
noted. Every power, SAR and B1 value is as openEMS computed it at the tutorial's own (arbitrary, tiny) excitation
unless its name ends `_per_w` or `_per_sqrtw`, which are per watt accepted at the feed, as the tutorial normalises.

### `Dipole_SAR/` — run 1 of R-sar1-5's five

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Dipole_SAR/sar_dipole.xml` | the CSXCAD XML the script wrote: geometry, materials, port, dumps and **the grid lines SAR-7 runs on** (114 × 115 × 116 lines) |
| `Dipole_SAR/freq_hz.npy` | the script's own frequency vector: 501 points, 0.5–1.5 GHz |
| `Dipole_SAR/s11.npy` | S11 = uf_ref / uf_inc over it, complex |
| `Dipole_SAR/zin_ohm.npy` | Zin = uf_tot / if_tot, complex |
| `Dipole_SAR/p_acc_w.npy` | the port's accepted power |
| `Dipole_SAR/sar_10g.npy` | `SAR_10g.h5`, the 10 g IEEE_62704 average `sar_calc` made of the raw dump, W/kg, (83, 90, 91), float32 |
| `Dipole_SAR/sar_10g_mesh_x_m.npy`, `Dipole_SAR/sar_10g_mesh_y_m.npy`, `Dipole_SAR/sar_10g_mesh_z_m.npy` | its mesh lines |
| `Dipole_SAR/summary.json` | the printed scalars, the SAR file's attributes (`maxSAR`, `power`, `mass`, cube counts), Zin at f0, the stop timestep |
| `Dipole_SAR/run-to-run.json` | R-sar1-5: the five runs' stop step and scalars |
| `Dipole_SAR/port_ut_1`, `Dipole_SAR/port_it_1` | the port's time-domain probes, so any other frequency vector can be evaluated |
| `Dipole_SAR/run.log` | the run's console output; `figures/` the script's three plots |

**Also kept, though the table does not list it:** the raw `DumpType 29` file `SAR.h5` (E, σ, ρ and cell volume on
the dump box's 83 × 90 × 91 cells, 24.5 MB; 9.3 MB as xz), as `Dipole_SAR/SAR_raw_dump29.h5`. A test that needs it
skips with a reason when it is absent. To make it
again, re-run the dipole with `--keep-raw` (below). A re-run stops at a different timestep (R-sar1-5), so its raw
dump matches `sar_10g.npy` to the run-to-run spread, not exactly; for an exact pair, re-run and keep both.

### `MRI_Loop_Coil/`

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/MRI_Loop_Coil.xml` | the CSXCAD XML the script wrote, with **the grid lines SAR-8 runs on** (154 × 122 × 162 lines). Its `DiscFile` names the bundled phantom under `${OPENEMS_INSTALL}`, this machine's install prefix |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/freq_hz.npy` | the script's own vector: 501 points, f0 ± fc = −2 to 598 MHz, a 1.2 MHz step (its first point is a negative frequency, as written) |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/s11.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/zin_ohm.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/p_acc_w.npy` | as for the dipole (Yin = 1 / Zin) |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xy.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xz.npy` | the local SAR planes (`SAR_xy.h5`, `SAR_xz.h5`, dump type 20), W/kg at the run's excitation, (113, 101, 1) and (113, 1, 137), float32 |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xy_mesh_x_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xy_mesh_y_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xy_mesh_z_m.npy` | the axial plane's mesh lines |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xz_mesh_x_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xz_mesh_y_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/sar_xz_mesh_z_m.npy` | the sagittal plane's |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1p_xy_t_per_sqrtw.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1m_xy_t_per_sqrtw.npy` | B1+ and B1− on the axial plane, T per √W accepted, exactly as the script computed them, (113, 101) |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1p_xz_t_per_sqrtw.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1m_xz_t_per_sqrtw.npy` | the same on the sagittal plane, (113, 137) |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1_xy_mesh_x_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1_xy_mesh_y_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1_xz_mesh_x_m.npy`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/b1_xz_mesh_z_m.npy` | the H dumps' mesh lines |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/summary.json` | accepted power, the S11 minimum, Yin at f0, peak local SAR per watt on each plane, the SAR files' attributes |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/port_ut_1`, `MRI_Loop_Coil/port_it_1` | the port's time-domain probes: **SAR-8's 0.5 MHz S11 gate is finer than the script's 1.2 MHz step**, so it evaluates S11 from these |
| `MRI_Loop_Coil/run.log` | the run's console output; `figures/` the script's five plots |

### `MRI_LP_Birdcage/`

The grid is **cylindrical** (r, α, z): mesh lines `_1` are r in metres, `_2` α in radians (a closed circle: the last
line is the first plus 2π, as the script reads it with `CloseAlpha`), `_3` z in metres. The script reads one plane,
the dump cell nearest z = 0, which is z = 1.25 mm.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/BirdCage.xml` | the openEMS XML the script wrote with `WriteOpenEMS`: **the whole setup**, FDTD settings and excitation included, and the grid SAR-8's birdcage follow-up runs on (65 r × 305 α (304 cells, closed) × 219 z lines). Its `DiscFile` names the bundled body phantom under `${OPENEMS_INSTALL}` |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/freq_hz.npy` | the script's vector: 201 points, 0–150 MHz, a 0.75 MHz step |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/s11.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/s22.npy` | as the script computes them. **Both ports are driven**, so each includes the other's coupling (the script says they may exceed 0 dB) |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port1_uf_inc.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port1_uf_ref.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port1_uf_tot.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port1_if_tot.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port1_p_acc_w.npy` | port 1's voltages, current and accepted power over that vector |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port2_uf_inc.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port2_uf_ref.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port2_uf_tot.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port2_if_tot.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port2_p_acc_w.npy` | port 2's (driven at −j, as a delay of a quarter period) |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/sar_z0.npy` | local SAR on the plane (`SAR.h5`, dump type 20), W/kg at the run's excitation, (49, 305) |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/sar_z0_mesh_1.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/sar_z0_mesh_2.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/sar_z0_mesh_3.npy` | its mesh lines |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/b1p_z0_t.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/b1m_z0_t.npy` | B1+ and B1− in T at the run's excitation, exactly as the script computed them from Br, Bα (`docs/design/sar.md` §1.5), r ≤ 0.1 m, (40, 305) |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/b1_z0_mesh_1.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/b1_z0_mesh_2.npy`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/b1_z0_mesh_3.npy` | their mesh lines |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/summary.json` | values at the frequency point nearest f0 (128.25 MHz), the S11 minimum, and two values **the converter derives** rather than the script (`_derived`: per watt accepted at both ports together) |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port_ut1`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port_ut2`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port_it1`, `MRI_LP_Birdcage/port_it2` | the ports' time-domain probes (the script's own sampling) |
| `MRI_LP_Birdcage/run.log` | the run's console output; `figures/` the script's three plots |

### `analytic/`

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `analytic/unittest.log` | `test_sar_analytic.py` under unittest, verbose: 6 tests, OK |
| `analytic/uniform_in_e.npy`, `analytic/uniform_in_conductivity.npy`, `analytic/uniform_in_density.npy`, `analytic/uniform_in_volume.npy`, `analytic/uniform_in_mesh_x_m.npy`, `analytic/uniform_in_mesh_y_m.npy`, `analytic/uniform_in_mesh_z_m.npy`, `analytic/uniform_out_sar.npy` | the 4 × 4 × 4 uniform phantom (σ 0.5 S/m, ρ 1000 kg/m³, Ex 1 V/m peak, 1 mm cells) and its local SAR from the installed `sar_calc`, `--mass 0`: 2.5e-4 W/kg in every cell |
| `analytic/random_in_e.npy`, `analytic/random_in_conductivity.npy`, `analytic/random_in_density.npy`, `analytic/random_in_volume.npy`, `analytic/random_in_mesh_x_m.npy`, `analytic/random_in_mesh_y_m.npy`, `analytic/random_in_mesh_z_m.npy`, `analytic/random_out_sar.npy` | the 10 × 10 × 10 thread-consistency phantom (σ uniform in [0.1, 1.0] from `RandomState(42)`, 2 mm cells) and its 1 g IEEE_62704 average |
| `analytic/uniform_sar_calc.log`, `analytic/random_sar_calc.log` | `sar_calc`'s output. The random phantom holds 8 g in all, so a 1 g cube does not fit everywhere, and `sar_calc` prints `can't find fitting cubical averaging volume` for each direction it cannot fit one at an unused voxel (`docs/design/sar.md` §1.3); that is its own behaviour |

`e` is the dump's (3, nx, ny, nz) complex field; the mesh lines are the dump's cell centres.

## Commands

From the repository root, with openEMS's venv Python (`~/opt/openEMS/venv/bin/python`) and `T` the openEMS-Project
checkout's `openEMS/python/Tutorials`:

```
python testdata/sar/openems-ref/tools/run_python_example.py Dipole_SAR    $T/Dipole_SAR.py    ${SIM_ROOT} <out dir> [--keep-raw]
python testdata/sar/openems-ref/tools/run_python_example.py MRI_Loop_Coil $T/MRI_Loop_Coil.py ${SIM_ROOT} <out dir>
python testdata/sar/openems-ref/tools/run_analytic.py ${OPENEMS_PROJECT}/openEMS/python/Tests ~/opt/openEMS/bin/sar_calc <scratch> testdata/sar/openems-ref/analytic
octave --no-gui --norc testdata/sar/openems-ref/tools/run_birdcage.m ${OPENEMS_PROJECT}/openEMS/matlab/Tutorials/MRI_LP_Birdcage.m \
       ${SIM_ROOT} <out dir> ~/opt/openEMS/share/openEMS/matlab ~/opt/openEMS/share/CSXCAD/matlab ~/opt/openEMS/bin/openEMS [setup-only]
python testdata/sar/openems-ref/tools/birdcage_to_npy.py <out dir>
```

What each wrapper replaces, and nothing else: the plot backend (Agg, figures saved rather than shown), the geometry
viewer call (skipped), and where the script's temporary directory is. `run_python_example.py --exact-endcriteria`
exists for R-sar1-5 only and was not used for any kept reference. Then `<out dir>` was copied here, with the
port probes and the console log beside it, and this machine's paths replaced by `${OPENEMS_INSTALL}`,
`${OPENEMS_PROJECT}` and `${SIM_ROOT}`. The tutorials' warning that their optional voxel body model is absent names
that model and its file; those words are redacted in the logs (overview L2: a restricted model is never named here).

**The two Python examples' FDTD settings live in the scripts, not in their XML** (CSX writes only the
structure and its grid); the birdcage's XML holds them all:

| | Dipole_SAR | MRI_Loop_Coil | MRI_LP_Birdcage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time steps, end criterion | at most 30,000; 1e-4 (−40 dB) | default (1e9); 1e-4 | default; 1e-4 |
| `CellConstantMaterial` | on | on | on |
| Excitation | Gaussian, f0 0, fc 1.5 GHz | Gaussian, f0 298 MHz, fc 300 MHz | Gaussian, f0 75 MHz, fc 75 MHz |
| Boundaries | PML_8 on all six faces | MUR on all six | PEC in r⁺ (the bore shield), PML in ±z with 10 lines added for it, none in r⁻ and ±α (a full cylinder); cylindrical, multigrid at 10 and 20 mm |
| Feed | lumped port, 50 Ω, z | lumped port, 2.5 Ω, y, in the bottom strip gap | two lumped ports, 50 Ω, z, amplitudes 1 and −j as delays |

| Run | Cells | Time step | Steps | Stopped by | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dipole_SAR run 1 (the reference) | 1,520,760 | 4.66e-12 s | 2,272 | end criterion, at −46.15 dB | 28.3 s, all cores; 142 MC/s |
| MRI_Loop_Coil | 3,043,656 | 3.39e-12 s | 77,409 | end criterion, at −40.51 dB | 265.6 s; 900 MC/s |
| MRI_LP_Birdcage | 4,023,030 (cylindrical, multigrid) | 3.65e-13 s | 225,918 | end criterion, at −40.49 dB | 3,170 s (53 min); 288 MC/s on 4 threads, the engine's own choice |
| analytic | — | — | — | — | 0.3 s |

## The rule

**Nothing here is regenerated by circuitRF.** A re-run on a later openEMS is a new reference set: run it beside this
one, compare, and record what moved and why in `docs/design/sar.md`, as `testdata/em3d/f0` is treated.
